scenes.heading: Building a repeatable client onboarding process

sents.d: Building a repeatable client onboarding process
A defined intake process produces better briefs and fewer surprises.

A vague starting brief ('make it pop,' 'something modern') is one of the biggest sources of wasted revision rounds — a structured intake process front-loads the clarifying questions instead of discovering them mid-project.

A simple onboarding questionnaire covering the client's audience, competitors, things they like and dislike visually, and any non-negotiable brand elements gives you a much stronger starting point than an open-ended request.
Following the questionnaire with a short kickoff call to walk through the answers together often surfaces additional context that wouldn't have come through in writing alone.

take: Ask the right questions before you design anything.
